$comment: Hand-written stand-in for `prism --help --json`. Replaced, not edited, once the CLI emits its own description. Verbs and flags follow the agreed v1.0 verb list.

globalFlags.meaning: Print the result as one JSON object instead of text.
Enable one experimental feature by name for this invocation.
Print usage for the verb and exit 0.

exitCodes.name: pass
exitCodes.meaning: The verb did what you asked and every check it ran passed.

exitCodes.name: fail
exitCodes.meaning: A check failed, an intent sentence is unproved, or a replay diverged.

exitCodes.name: cannot verify
exitCodes.meaning: No verdict was reached: a missing attestation, an unreachable registry or an unknown format revision.

prismCode.$comment: What ships today: the prism-code command as published on npm. A test compares these verbs with the command's own --help, so the list cannot drift from the binary.
prismCode.needs: Node.js 22 or later. build, verify and conformance also need Docker and a `prismpm.lock` in the current directory.

exitCodes.name: ok
exitCodes.meaning: The verb did what you asked, or `check` reached a verdict the policy accepts.

exitCodes.name: vectors failed
exitCodes.meaning: At least one acceptance vector did not replay or the holo carries none, `verify-attestation` did not verify, `check` reached a verdict the policy rejects, or `pull` found a digest that does not match or a holo that fails verification and wrote nothing.

exitCodes.name: refused
exitCodes.meaning: The holo, capability file or manifest cannot be read or fails its checks, an identity check failed, a guest import, the holo's world or a provider is not granted, or a provider failed; or `check` reached no verdict: not a holo, an unreadable policy or an unknown format revision; or `push` or `pull` got no answer: an unreachable registry, refused credentials, a reference that does not exist or referrers that cannot be stored; or an export's bytes differ from the build manifest.

exitCodes.name: signing failed
exitCodes.meaning: `attest` could not sign, or the optional sigstore packages are not installed.

exitCodes.name: proof mismatch
exitCodes.meaning: `run` refused a holo for a proof reason. 11 is a world mismatch, 12 a determinism violation, 13 a replay error.

exitCodes.name: usage
exitCodes.meaning: The arguments were wrong, or `prismpm.lock` is missing.

exitCodes.name: no Docker
exitCodes.meaning: Docker is not installed or not on the PATH.

exitCodes.name: untyped
exitCodes.meaning: Dispatch threw something untyped: a guest trap, or a bug in the runtime.

verbs.name: run
verbs.summary: Check the holo against the policy. With an input, this is one run as a container: dispatch the input, print the output and exit with the container's code, keeping the container until `rm` unless `--rm`. Without one, serve its view on a local port; a POST to `/_hologram/intent` dispatches one request. A holo that fails check is refused unless `--allow-unverified`, which warns on every start.

verbs.name: rm
verbs.summary: Remove containers, by id or unique id prefix. A running container is refused.

verbs.name: init
verbs.summary: Scaffold a project: `prism.toml`, a language-1.2 model and its Lean workspace. With `--sdk-image`, also copy that image's `standards.lock` and write `prismpm.lock` (needs Docker). `npm create prism-code` runs the same command.

verbs.name: manifest
verbs.summary: Check and lint the project's `prism.toml`, with the overlay for the target merged in, and print the application, the grant and the variables.

verbs.name: providers
verbs.summary: `up` runs the `prism-provider-<type>` each capability in `prism.toml` declares and prints the variables it produced, and `down` releases them. Text output names them, and `--json` also prints their values. The capability set must allow the type and each variable. Experimental.

verbs.name: vectors
verbs.summary: Replay every acceptance vector the holo carries and exit 1 on a failure.

verbs.name: inspect
verbs.summary: Print what the holo says about itself, without running it, or a container's state, exit code, image digest and output.

verbs.name: attest
verbs.summary: Sign an in-toto statement about the holo into its attestation section: keyless with an OIDC token, or with `--key`.

verbs.name: verify-attestation
verbs.summary: Check the holo's attestations against the signer you expect, or against `--key`.

verbs.name: export
verbs.summary: Write a release's six-file browser export or tarball, byte-checked against the build manifest, attestations beside.

verbs.name: check
verbs.summary: Judge the holo against a policy and print its verdict: the assurance level, whether the policy passed, and every reason. `--policy` takes a Rego file, the name of a shipped policy (`pure-only`, `provenance-only`) or a JSON file. Exit 1 when the policy denies, 2 when it cannot be parsed or evaluated. Without a holo, the deprecated spelling of `build --check`, removed in 0.4.0.

verbs.name: push
verbs.summary: Put the holo in an OCI registry or a local store as a deterministic manifest, each attestation a referrer. With `--key` or `--keyless`, also sign a statement naming the manifest, so `cosign verify-attestation` passes on the same reference.

verbs.name: pull
verbs.summary: Fetch a holo and write it only after its digests, archive, verdict and attestations pass; the signer flags are those of `verify-attestation`. A reference is `registry/repo:tag`, `@sha256:`, `@blake3:` or `dir://`.

verbs.name: build
verbs.summary: Build the project into a holo inside the SDK image the lockfile pins. With `--check`, validate the model and write nothing.

verbs.name: verify
verbs.summary: Run verify in the SDK image the lockfile pins.

verbs.name: conformance
verbs.summary: Run the conformance suite in the SDK image the lockfile pins.

providers.$comment: Provider services (#294, experimental). The wire protocol is on the manifest reference page.
providers.discovery: An executable named `prism-provider-<type>` on the PATH is found the way a plugin is, and is not a plugin: `prism-code provider-<type>` is not a command, and the `provider-` prefix is reserved.

firstParty.name: kv
firstParty.usage: provider = { type = "kv", options = { store, dir, set } }
firstParty.summary: A local key-value store, kept as one JSON file under `.prism/kv`. Returns `URL` and `STORE`. `up` never overwrites a key, and `down` deletes the file. Ships in the prism-code package.

plugins.$comment: CLI plugins (#293, experimental). `--help` prints them under a Plugins heading, apart from the verbs above.
plugins.discovery: An executable named `prism-<name>` on the PATH runs as `prism-code <name>`, and `prism <name>` once the CLI is renamed. On Windows the first `PATHEXT` extension found in a directory wins and names are case-insensitive. The first PATH directory that has the plugin wins, and a built-in verb always wins over a plugin.
plugins.contract: A plugin answers `prism-<name> prism-cli-plugin-metadata` with JSON: `schemaVersion` "1", `vendor`, `version`, `shortDescription` and optional `errorHooks`, a list of verbs. A plugin that does not answer is listed as invalid and never runs. Arguments reach the plugin unchanged and its exit code is the command's.
plugins.hooks: When a verb a plugin names in `errorHooks` exits non-zero, prism-code runs `prism-<name> prism-cli-plugin-hooks` with `{"schemaVersion":"1","command","args","exitCode"}` on stdin and prints the `messages` it returns under What's next, at most ten lines. Set `PRISM_CODE_NO_HOOKS=1` to turn hooks off.

firstParty.name: doctor
firstParty.summary: Check Node.js, Docker, `./prismpm.lock` and the optional sigstore packages; exit 1 when a check fails. Ships in the prism-code package, and its error hook points at it when check, build, verify, conformance or export-browser exit 64 or 69.

verbs.name: init
verbs.summary: Scaffold a new application: `prism.toml`, `examples/`, `intent.md`, a default capability set and the lockfile.

flags.meaning: Which type source the scaffold writes.
Starting examples and intent.
Overwrite files that already exist.

verbs.name: build
verbs.summary: Compile the model into a holo inside the pinned SDK image, record provenance and the proof attestation, and cache the result by spec digest.

flags.meaning: How much the provenance records. `max` adds every resolved input and the full toolchain environment.
Skip provenance. Unsafe: the holo cannot pass `check` above P0.
Rebuild even when the spec digest is unchanged.
Apply the matching overlay, `prism.browser.toml` or `prism.node.toml`.
How many times the agent may revise the model before the build fails.

verbs.name: check
verbs.summary: Verify the holo's digest, provenance, proof, lockfile pins and declared world against a policy, then print a verdict with the assurance level and reasons.

flags.meaning: Policy to judge against.
Do not contact the transparency log or any registry. Missing data exits 2.

verbs.name: run
verbs.summary: Instantiate the holo after `check` passes at the policy's level, then grant exactly the capability set it declares.

flags.meaning: One input to dispatch. Omit it to read inputs line by line.
Policy the gate judges against.
Run even when `check` fails. Prints a warning on every start.
Remove the container when it exits. One input only.
Serve the instance over HTTP instead of dispatching once.

verbs.name: dev
verbs.summary: Watch the model, rebuild and re-check on every change, and serve a local studio with Check and Replay tabs.

flags.meaning: Studio port.
Do not open the studio in a browser.
Policy the Check tab judges against.

verbs.name: replay
verbs.summary: Re-execute a recorded history against the current build and fail on the first divergence.

flags.meaning: Which holo to replay against.
Continue past the first divergence and report every one.

verbs.name: push
verbs.summary: Push a holo and its attestations to an OCI registry. The attestations travel as referrers of the holo.

flags.meaning: Push to a local directory store instead of a registry.
Push the holo only. The pushed holo checks at P0.

verbs.name: pull
verbs.summary: Pull a holo and its attestations from an OCI registry or a local directory store.

flags.meaning: Pull from a local directory store.
Run `check` on the pulled holo and exit with its code.

verbs.name: deploy
verbs.summary: Publish the holo to a GitHub repository and GitHub Pages, serving its attestations alongside it.

flags.meaning: Repository to publish to.
Branch GitHub Pages serves.
Push the repository only.

verbs.name: export
verbs.summary: Write the six-file browser export, a tarball, or a runnable OCI image that `docker run` serves.

flags.meaning: Where the browser export is written.
Write one tarball instead of a directory.
Write a runnable OCI image under this name.

verbs.name: inspect
verbs.summary: Print the manifest, section digests, format revision, world and attestations of a holo without running it.

flags.meaning: Print one part only.
Print the security view: signers, trusted base, capability set, theorem list.
With `--audit`, write the report to a file.

verbs.name: attest
verbs.summary: Add a signed statement to a holo. Signing is keyless by default.

flags.meaning: JSON file holding the predicate.
Predicate type URI.
Sign with a local key for air-gapped use instead of keyless.

verbs.name: verify
verbs.summary: Check a signed statement on a holo against the signing identity you expect.

flags.meaning: Identity the statement must be signed by.
Issuer that identity must come from.
Verify statements of one predicate type only.
Verify against a local public key instead of keyless.

verbs.name: generate
verbs.summary: Regenerate the JS, Rust and Python bindings and the typed client from the world. Nothing is written when nothing changed.

flags.meaning: Output path.
Which bindings to write.

verbs.name: lock
verbs.summary: Write or refresh the lockfile from the current model and inputs, without building. Pins that still resolve stay as they are, and the SDK image and toolchain pins do not move. Exits 2 when there is no lockfile or its SDK cannot be resolved.

flags.meaning: Write nothing. Fail when the lockfile is stale and name the pins that differ.

verbs.name: update
verbs.summary: Move the lockfile forward and print the old and new digests of every pin that changed. Without a flag it refreshes the toolchain pins; with `--toolchain` it also pins a new SDK image. Exits 2 when the lockfile or the image cannot be resolved.

flags.meaning: SDK image to pin, as `name@sha256:digest`.
Standards lock the new image selects. Needs `--toolchain`.
Print the change without writing the lockfile.
